ā^phractus , i, f., or ā^phractum , i, n., = ἄφρακτος (uncovered, sc. ναῦς, hence),
I.a long vessel without a deck (in pure Latin, navis aperta; “only in Cic.): Navigavimus tardius propter aphractorum Rhodiorum imbecillitatem,” Cic. Att. 5, 13, 1 : “detraxit viginti ipsos dies aphractus Rhodiorum,” id. ib. 6, 8, 4 : “aphracta Rhodiorum habebam,” id. ib. 5, 11, 4 ; so id. ib. 5, 12, 1.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
